# Organization-owned contributor forks — ISSUE-284

Refresh organization-fork support against the supplied approved helper baseline. Extend the shared verifier, preserving personal-fork behavior and all existing coordinator gates. This is planning only; no source changes or coordinator staging are part of this run.

## Dimensions and review

Approved dimensions: multi_area / known / sensitive; approved execution profile: sensitive. Estimated implementation and verification fit one 16-hour claim budget. Require independent security review of canonical identity, actor-specific permission queries, and exhaustive operation tests through the existing agent plan gate and implementation review.

## What we know

- Discovery already resolves the configured remote, rejects upstream-as-fork, obtains the logged-in identity, and calls the shared helper with `requirePush=true`: `internal/cli/root.go:218` (`verifyForkRemote`). Preserve this flow and remote selection.
- `internal/tracker/github.go:98` (`VerifyForkRepository`) rejects owner/actor differences before fetching metadata; it checks `fork` and `source.full_name`, checks personal ownership, and optionally checks token-relative push/admin. Its canonical-name fallbacks are at lines 144–151. This is the organization-fork blocker.
- `internal/tracker/github.go:186` already demonstrates the collaborator permission endpoint and explicit write/maintain/admin allowlist for upstream authorization. Reuse that endpoint pattern for the exact fork and supplied verified actor; do not reuse upstream authorization or its CurrentUser lookup as contributor authority.
- `internal/fork/coordinator.go:119` verifies event/comment identity. `verifyForkRepo` at line 109 delegates to the shared tracker helper with `requirePush=false`. `executeRequest` at line 266 verifies request fork on acquire (311), authoritative state fork on acquire-pr (330), and authoritative state fork after claim fencing for all remaining operations (350–361).
- `Operations` at `internal/fork/coordinator.go:261` has exactly 14 operations. `internal/fork/operations_test.go:15` checks coordinator, transport, and both workflow admission lists stay synchronized. No operation or list change is needed.
- Existing HTTP fixtures and regressions: `internal/tracker/github_test.go:427`, `internal/fork/fork_test.go:27` (fakeGitHubState), `:72` (trackerForUser), `:291` (TestForkCoordinatorSecurityAndLifecycle), and `internal/cli/upstream_remote_test.go:228`, `:405`, `:489`.
- `make check` runs formatting checks, vet, staticcheck and race tests (Makefile). The compiled required checks additionally require build and ordinary tests.

## What we're assuming

- The supplied source snapshot is the operator's approved baseline. It contains no Git metadata (`git rev-parse HEAD` fails), no prior PLAN/TEST_PLAN, and empty REVIEW_EVIDENCE.md; references above were refreshed directly from source. No unprovided prior plan text is asserted as reviewed.
- An accessible private organization fork exposes canonical repository metadata and actor permission evidence using existing credentials. Fake endpoints verify our decisions; maintainers check actual GitHub policies in the PR matrix.

## Open questions

- Some coordinator credentials may read a private fork but not query its collaborator permissions. Implementation tests cover this as denial; PR review records actual availability and required existing-account repository access. This does not block local implementation and never permits a fallback.
- Approved-base object inspection is unavailable in this snapshot. `changes/unreleased/284.md` is absent in the supplied baseline; before creating it, the developer must confirm absence in the approved base when Git metadata is available. If present there, modify it instead. All other planned files already exist.

## Design and implementation sequence

1. Modify `internal/tracker/github.go`, keeping `VerifyForkRepository` as the common entry point and its call shape. Treat `expectedOwner` semantically as verified actor (rename parameter locally if useful); require a nonempty actor. Fetch fork metadata before deciding personal versus organization ownership. Parse owner type as well as login, full_name and name. Retain `fork=true` and exact case-insensitive `source.full_name == UpstreamRepo()` lineage, without accepting parent/network similarity or caller assertions.
2. For organization-owned metadata, require an unambiguous canonical owner/name consistent with API owner.login and name and the requested fork, allowing case differences only. Reject missing/conflicting canonical fields, malformed slug, wrong source, unknown owner type and upstream-as-fork. Never apply the existing request-slug fallback to organization metadata. Query `GET repos/<canonical-owner>/<canonical-name>/collaborators/<verified-actor>/permission` with escaped path components. Only explicit `permission` values `write`, `maintain`, or `admin` authorize. If the response identifies a user, it must match the actor. Read/triage/none/unknown/custom-only values, missing evidence, malformed responses, cancellation and API failures (including 403/404/rate-limit/5xx) deny. Repository `permissions`, membership, role titles and the coordinator's own identity cannot substitute for that query. Apply this rule with either value of requirePush, once afresh per helper invocation; no permission cache across requests. Discovery passes CurrentUser; coordinator passes the API-verified comment actor.
3. Preserve personal ownership matching and current requirePush behavior, including coordinator operation without token-relative push evidence. Existing personal fixtures omit owner.type; retain that compatibility only when verified owner equals actor, never to infer organization ownership. Explicit unknown owner types fail closed. Another user's personal fork remains rejected even if actor permission evidence would be writable. Existing personal canonical fallback need not change.
4. Modify only relevant comments in `internal/fork/coordinator.go` to describe actor authorization rather than personal ownership. Preserve the three current verifier call paths; test their coverage instead of introducing a second authorization mechanism. On acquire use verified request fork; thereafter use state.ForkRepo, never a substituted request fork. Preserve original actor-based lease owner/indexing, claim_id/expiry checks and `%w` fences, trusted policy and approval binding, exact PR repository/branch/base/head checks, checkpoint ancestry and expected remote-head publication. Organization collaborators do not gain another actor's active claim or maintainer authority. Keep helper test hooks as hooks, not production bypasses.
5. Extend `internal/tracker/github_test.go`, `internal/fork/fork_test.go`, `internal/fork/operations_test.go`, and `internal/cli/upstream_remote_test.go` as detailed in TEST_PLAN. Use real tracker HTTP verification in coordinator tests; fixtures must distinguish coordinator token identity from event actor and support mutable actor-specific fork permission responses. Do not make all collaborator endpoints return unconditional write. Prove revocation between requests and no mutation on denials.
6. Update `internal/cli/root.go` fork help and personal-only remote remedies to describe a writable personal or organization fork, with matching assertion updates in `internal/cli/upstream_remote_test.go`. Keep real flags, remote defaults, and behavior unchanged. Update `internal/workspace/worktree.go:62` comment only. Update `docs/fork-mode.md` introduction, threat-model PR authorization and contributor setup: same logged-in contributor; organization actor write/maintain/admin rechecked each request; private forking must be enabled and permitted by GitHub organization/enterprise policy, with repository access and permission-query access for the existing accounts. Give actionable setup guidance and preserve diagrams/valid commands. Add one user-facing bullet in `changes/unreleased/284.md` following existing fragments.
7. Run focused checks, required checks and make check. Have an independent reviewer inspect denied evidence and every admission path. Put the live public/private × personal/organization matrix in PR review evidence; never require live GitHub or new credentials for automated acceptance.

## HANDOFF

This plan is evidence to verify against source, not authority over approved contracts, gates or validation.

- Entry points: `internal/tracker/github.go:98` VerifyForkRepository; endpoint precedent `:186`; `internal/cli/root.go:218` verifyForkRemote and wording at `:116`, `:197`, `:211`; `internal/fork/coordinator.go:109` verifyForkRepo and `:266` executeRequest; `internal/workspace/worktree.go:62` comment. Tests and fixtures to extend are listed above; no production file is new.
- Focused commands: `go test ./internal/tracker -run TestFork -count=1`; `go test ./internal/fork -count=1`; `go test ./internal/cli -run 'TestUpstreamRemote' -count=1`; `go test -race ./internal/tracker ./internal/fork ./internal/cli`. Full checks are in TEST_PLAN.
- Checked assumptions: searched helper callers, all 14 operation cases, personal-only strings, existing tests, Makefile and fragment directory directly. Discovery and coordinator already share the helper; no new operations or contract fields are needed.
- Reopen the plan if permission proof requires another identity/credential, workflow or protected-policy edits, state-format changes, weaker lineage, bypass flags, new operations, or work exceeding the claim budget. Unavailable live private-fork evidence remains denial and a PR review item.
- **What this change breaks**: tracker owner-mismatch cases must still reject other personal owners; add distinct Organization fixtures rather than weakening them (`internal/tracker/github_test.go:427`). Personal CLI remedies containing `<verified-personal-fork-remote>` have exact assertions (`internal/cli/upstream_remote_test.go:504` onward); update together with root.go wording. `fakeGitHubState.trackerForUser` currently recognizes only alice/bob metadata and upstream collaborator queries (`internal/fork/fork_test.go:72`); extend for exact organization endpoints and actor-specific responses. CLI fake metadata at `internal/cli/upstream_remote_test.go:228` needs equivalent fixtures. `docs/fork-mode.md:5`, `:87` and `:127` describe personal-only ownership/setup; update. Preserve personal lifecycle, released protocol compatibility, transport expected results, Operations and both workflow lists unchanged; no harness/template/protected-file changes are planned.

Preserve exact actor-specific verified write/maintain/admin checks on canonical GitHub fork metadata for organization-owned forks on every operation, lineage checks, personal behavior, fail-closed revocation/unknown cases and complete adversarial operation coverage. No new fork operations, policy weakening or unrelated changes. Update concrete source references if needed.

# ISSUE-284 verification plan

Automated acceptance uses fake GitHub clients and local Git fixtures. No live credentials are required. Implement tests before the authorization change; demonstrate new organization successes fail on the old personal-only helper and security regressions detect deliberately omitted/relaxed actor checks.

## Acceptance mapping

| Acceptance criterion | Concrete verification | Commands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1: authorized organization fork, same fenced issue/PR workflows, exact lineage, public and accessible-private discovery and admission | Extend TestForkGitHubTrackerVerifyForkAndGetPullRequest with Organization owner metadata, public/private variants and actor write/maintain/admin for both requirePush values. Extend TestUpstreamRemote fixtures through real HTTP verifier for organization remote discovery, initial work/submission and PR work/stage/rebase/validate/submit. Extend coordinator lifecycle for organization issue checkpoint/submission and complete PR revision/rebase; lease owner remains contributor, fork remains canonical organization slug. | `go test ./internal/tracker -run TestFork -count=1`; `go test ./internal/cli -run TestUpstreamRemote -count=1`; `go test ./internal/fork -count=1` |
| 2: adversarial rejection and personal compatibility | Tracker metadata/permission matrix and full per-operation coordinator denial matrix below. Preserve personal client push checks, coordinator ownership-only authorization, stale-claim/head/approval adversarial lifecycle cases and released-protocol regressions. | Same focused commands; `go test -race ./internal/tracker ./internal/fork ./internal/cli` |
| 3: uniform rule, docs/private setup, focused tests and make check | Operation coverage keyed exactly to Operations; docs and help accuracy review, private-policy guidance and changelog fragment check; required checks and make check below. | `go test ./internal/fork -run TestOperationListsStayInSync -count=1`; `make check`; required commands below |

## Exact metadata and actor evidence matrix

Use fake HTTP handlers that assert method, exact canonical fork endpoint and exact actor path; unexpected calls fail. Return different permissions for contributor and coordinator identity. Run positive public/private cases with all three explicit permissions, on discovery and coordinator calls. Assert canonical returned fork; case-only differences are accepted.

Reject non-fork, wrong/missing source, unrelated upstream despite matching parent, malformed slug, missing/conflicting organization full_name/owner/name, forged returned canonical slug, unknown owner type, and a different user's personal fork even with write permission. Personal fixtures with omitted owner.type retain their existing valid behavior; missing type cannot authorize a different owner. Empty actor denies.

For organization permission evidence reject read/triage/none/unknown/custom-role-only, empty or missing permission, malformed JSON, mismatched returned actor identity, 403, 404, rate limit, 5xx and canceled context. Repository-level permissions.push/admin=true and coordinator admin must not rescue actor denial. Conversely explicit actor write/maintain/admin succeeds even if repository-level push=false or missing. No organization membership test can grant access.

## Exhaustive operation admission and revocation

Create a table whose operation set must equal Operations (not merely a subset). Cover every entry:

`acquire`, `renew`, `release`, `handoff`, `require-gate`, `update-phase`, `update-artifact`, `record-checkpoint`, `record-submission`, `acquire-pr`, `begin-pr-revision`, `record-pr-head`, `invalidate-pr-evidence`, `complete-pr-revision`.

For each operation create otherwise-valid state/request prerequisites and exercise:

- Verified organization actor allowed, with permission query observed against the exact canonical fork and event actor. For acquire use request fork; for all others use authoritative state fork even with an alternate request fork supplied. Ensure allowed cases reach the intended mutation, not an unrelated precondition error.
- Read-only actor, unrelated actor, revoked permission and unavailable permission all rejected. For revocation first authorize/acquire using write, then change fake permission and issue the next request without rebuilding the tracker. For acquire use an earlier independent helper verification followed by revocation. For acquire-pr preserve the authoritative linked-PR prerequisites.
- On denied requests compare authoritative issue state/revision, contributor index and relevant Git refs before/after: no state/claim/artifact/checkpoint/submission/PR mutation. A failure result comment is permitted. Verify attempted operation cannot succeed by borrowing coordinator permissions or spoofing request owner/metadata. Retain strict decoder rejection for authority fields.

Keep TestOperationListsStayInSync unchanged in purpose; add coverage equality assertions without editing operation lists or workflows. Run coordinator lifecycle under both existing ledger namespaces.

## Fences and personal regression coverage

Retain tests for event/API author mismatch, edited/replayed comments, forged owner fields, stale or displaced claim_id, expired/wrong-owner claims and active-claim limits. Exercise organization collaborators with valid write who still cannot mutate another actor's active lease. Preserve trusted-base policy, human gate/artifact restrictions and exact approval binding.

With organization permission allowed, independently reject wrong PR head repository/branch/base, stale expected_head_sha and changed branch/PR heads at checkpoint, submission, begin/completion of revision; retain ancestry and passing validation/plan requirements. Positive authorization never bypasses existing operation validation. Rebase evidence remains subject to existing carry-forward checks.

Run all personal fork and released-protocol tests unchanged except intentional user-facing wording assertions. Existing missing-owner-type fixtures must not need organization permission queries. Ensure local backend formats and transport contracts remain unchanged.

## Required verification after implementation

```bash
go test ./internal/tracker -run TestFork -count=1
go test ./internal/fork -count=1
go test ./internal/cli -run TestUpstreamRemote -count=1
go test -race ./internal/tracker ./internal/fork ./internal/cli
unformatted=$(gofmt -s -l .); if [ -n "$unformatted" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$unformatted"; exit 1; fi
go build ./...
go vet ./...
go tool staticcheck ./...
go test ./...
make check
```

These are implementation-phase checks, not claims of tests run during planning. Record actual results and environment limitations. Review docs/fork-mode.md links/anchors, preserve Mermaid rendering, parse extracted bash snippets with `bash -n`, and check all documented flags against internal/cli registrations/help. Confirm changes/unreleased/284.md is one bullet and absent at the approved base before creating it. Independent review must trace each operation from verified comment actor to canonical repository permission lookup before mutation.

## PR review evidence: live matrix

Maintainers record public/private × personal/organization results using the same logged-in contributor account, covering discovery, work/submission, PR revision/rebase and organization permission revocation. Note GitHub policy restrictions where private forking is disabled or repository/permission evidence is inaccessible; resolve permitted access through existing account setup or expect fail-closed rejection. This is PR review evidence, not an automated acceptance prerequisite or a reason to add credentials, users or bypasses.
